title: The Power of Argument
text:
An argumentative essay is a type of writing in which the author takes a clear position on a debatable issue and defends it with evidence. Unlike a descriptive essay, its main purpose is not to describe, but to persuade the reader. A strong essay usually begins with a thesis statement, which summarizes the writer's main claim. Each body paragraph then develops one reason that supports that claim.

Writers must also anticipate objections from readers who hold opposing views. By acknowledging counterarguments and responding to them, the writer shows fairness and makes the essay more convincing. Weak essays, on the other hand, often ignore opposing evidence altogether. As a result, they can seem one-sided and easy to dismiss.

questions.text: According to the passage, what is the main purpose of an argumentative essay?
options: To describe a place or person in detail
To persuade the reader to accept a position
To tell a personal story in chronological order

questions.text: According to the passage, what does acknowledging counterarguments help the writer show?
What can the reader infer about a body paragraph that does not support the thesis?
options: It would probably make the essay more persuasive
It would probably weaken the essay's argument
It would probably turn the essay into a narrative
It would probably make the thesis statement unnecessary

questions.text: Why might an essay that ignores opposing evidence seem unconvincing to readers?
options: Readers may feel the writer has not considered other views
Readers always prefer very long essays
Opposing evidence is always false by definition
The thesis statement becomes a question

vocabulary.definition: to make someone agree with or believe something
the main claim that a writer states and defends in an essay
arguments that oppose a particular position
able to make people believe that something is true

paragraph_translations: Un ensayo argumentativo es un tipo de escritura en el que el autor adopta una posición clara sobre un tema debatible y la defiende con pruebas. A diferencia de un ensayo descriptivo, su propósito principal no es describir, sino persuadir al lector. Un ensayo sólido suele comenzar con una declaración de tesis, que resume la afirmación principal del escritor. Después, cada párrafo de desarrollo expone una razón que apoya esa afirmación.

Los escritores también deben anticipar las objeciones de los lectores que sostienen opiniones opuestas. Al reconocer los contraargumentos y responder a ellos, el autor demuestra imparcialidad y hace que el ensayo sea más convincente. Los ensayos débiles, en cambio, suelen ignorar por completo las pruebas en contra. Como resultado, pueden parecer unilaterales y fáciles de rechazar.
